original_query: select   i_item_id  ,i_item_desc  ,s_store_id  ,s_store_name  ,sum(ss_net_profit) as store_sales_profit  ,sum(sr_net_loss) as store_returns_loss  ,sum(cs_net_profit) as catalog_sales_profit  from  store_sales  ,store_returns  ,catalog_sales  ,date_dim d1  ,date_dim d2  ,date_dim d3  ,store  ,item  where  d1.d_moy = 8  and d1.d_year = 2001  and d1.d_date_sk = ss_sold_date_sk  and i_item_sk = ss_item_sk  and s_store_sk = ss_store_sk  and ss_customer_sk = sr_customer_sk  and ss_item_sk = sr_item_sk  and ss_ticket_number = sr_ticket_number  and sr_returned_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk  and d2.d_moy               between 8 and  8 + 2  and d2.d_year              = 2001  and sr_customer_sk = cs_bill_customer_sk  and sr_item_sk = cs_item_sk  and cs_sold_date_sk = d3.d_date_sk  and d3.d_moy               between 8 and  8 + 2  and d3.d_year              = 2001  group by  i_item_id  ,i_item_desc  ,s_store_id  ,s_store_name  order by  i_item_id  ,i_item_desc  ,s_store_id  ,s_store_name  limit 100;
rewritten_query:
SELECT i.i_item_id,
       i.i_item_desc,
       s.s_store_id,
       s.s_store_name,
       SUM(ss.ss_net_profit) AS store_sales_profit,
       SUM(sr.sr_net_loss)  AS store_returns_loss,
       SUM(cs.cs_net_profit) AS catalog_sales_profit
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN store_returns sr
  ON sr.sr_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
 AND sr.sr_item_sk     = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND sr.sr_ticket_number = ss.ss_ticket_number
JOIN catalog_sales cs
  ON cs.cs_bill_customer_sk = sr.sr_customer_sk
 AND cs.cs_item_sk          = sr.sr_item_sk
JOIN date_dim d1
  ON d1.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
JOIN date_dim d2
  ON d2.d_date_sk = sr.sr_returned_date_sk
JOIN date_dim d3
  ON d3.d_date_sk = cs.cs_sold_date_sk
JOIN store s
  ON s.s_store_sk = ss.ss_store_sk
JOIN item i
  ON i.i_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
WHERE d1.d_moy  = 8
  AND d1.d_year = 2001
  AND d2.d_moy  BETWEEN 8 AND 10
  AND d2.d_year = 2001
  AND d3.d_moy  BETWEEN 8 AND 10
  AND d3.d_year = 2001
GROUP BY i.i_item_id, i.i_item_desc, s.s_store_id, s.s_store_name
ORDER BY i.i_item_id, i.i_item_desc, s.s_store_id, s.s_store_name
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Fold the constant expression `8 + 2` into `10` in the d2/d3 date filters for clarity and guaranteed sargability (the previous CTE rewrite regressed cost by ~19%, so avoid materialized CTEs for date_dim; keeping date_dim joined inline preserves index scans on d_date_sk).

Convert implicit comma-style joins with WHERE-clause join predicates into explicit ANSI JOIN syntax, grouping each join's conditions together. This is semantically equivalent but eliminates the risk of accidental cartesian products and improves maintainability.

Keep the fact-table join order (store_sales -> store_returns -> catalog_sales) with join keys in ON clauses; keep date_dim/store/item as inline dimension joins rather than a shared CTE for d2/d3, since the previous CTE-based plan cost 42,546 vs 35,795 (the materialized CTE lost index access on d_date_sk). Additionally, consider covering indexes (e.g., on store_returns(sr_returned_date_sk, sr_item_sk, sr_ticket_number, sr_customer_sk) INCLUDE (sr_net_loss) and catalog_sales(cs_bill_customer_sk, cs_item_sk, cs_sold_date_sk) INCLUDE (cs_net_profit)) plus ANALYZE to address low row estimates (rows=1) observed in the plan.
